newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq oil export capacity can reach 6 mln barrels.
newsitem.headline: Iraq oil export capacity can reach 6 mln barrels.

text.p: Iraqi oil pipelines and facilities are able now to handle oil production and exports of six million barrels per day (bpd) that will be reached in five years once U.N. sanctions are lifted, a senior oil official said in remarks published on Saturday.

"Iraqi oil pipelines and the current capacities of ports have the ability to handle six million bpd after five years from the date the embargo on the country is removed," Sami Sharif, oil ministry undersecretary, told the government newspaper al-Jumhouriya.
He said to reach such a production level Iraq needed to develop ten large oilfields. He said all technical and practical aspects to realise such a level were available.
Sharif put Iraq's proven reserves at 112 billion barrels while probable reserves were 214 billion barrels.

Iraq concluded oil deals with Chinese, Russian and Turkish firms to develop oilfields in the north and south of the country. It has been negotiating with French and Italian companies to develop more fields.
The United Nations embargo imposed on Iraq for invading Kuwait in 1990 bars trade with Baghdad.
The embargo includes a ban on oil exports but the U.N. has allowed Iraq to pump $2 billion worth of oil over six months to international markets to buy urgent needs for Iraqis.

The first six months of the oil-for-food deal ended on June and another six months then started. Iraq has not yet exported oil for the second period, waiting for the U.N. to approve a food and distribution plan which it submitted to a U.N. office in Baghdad.
Sharif said the sanctions committee on Iraq was still holding 200 deals to buy food, medicine and other humanitarian goods. He blamed the committee's stand on the United States.
